title: The give-and-go: for two seconds after a mate takes your pass he looks for you first
pillar: P2 the pass is the fastest thing on the ice, and it pays (through the mates: no control switching, R-0038)
hypothesis: A pass pays in a one-skater game when it comes back to you in a better place or becomes a shot. Of the planning hand's completed passes at pro 36 % come back, 49 % are lost by the mate first, 12 % become his shot. E06 showed the mates' coin (pass_to_human) is not what holds the return back: the conditions in front of it are. thirdjam's own rule (JamAICore.cpp:1675-1730) returns the puck to an open human only when a coin falls (0.4 at pro), when the mate is not a back, and when the mate could not drive the net himself (lane A153 / A206: a driving mate passes only to a human set up for the one-timer); and the mate must happen to face him. The change (patch 0005, the brain's copy in the thirdlife tree; a tune key of the mates, mate.hk_give_go_frames_tl=120 at every level): for 120 frames after a mate takes a pass FROM THE HUMAN, the return to the open human (thirdjam's own test of open: on his feet, 5 to 25 m away, ahead of or level with the puck, 3 m of room round him, his lane free) needs no coin, is made by a back too, is not held back by the mate's own drive, and the mate turns to face him. A shot the mate has decided on still comes first. Expected: more of the completed passes come back (36 % toward 50 %), fewer are lost first; passes received a match up; the one-timer more often (the return finds a human going to the net); taking the pass away costs the planning hand (T3). Risk: the mate gives up a drive he should have finished; the puck goes back and forth and is cut.
tempo: none: no row of the tempo map moves

why: The puck did not come back more often. Of the planning hand's completed passes at pro the share that came back first: 35.5 to 35.0 % (regular), 39.3 to 33.3 (novice), 34.2 to 24.8 (good, whose mates shot more instead: 10.5 to 16.2 %); thirdjam's regular hand 33.9 to 32.3. The share lost first by the mate did not fall (49.6 to 52.5 % for the regular planning hand). Wins moved both ways inside or near the noise (planning hand at pro -5.0 +-6.5 / -6.7 +-4.7 / +6.7 +-3.2; thirdjam's +3.3 / +6.7 / +6.7), and the pass is still worth nothing to the hand (81.7 % with it, 83.3 without). The target did not move, so the rule is not kept and its patch is taken out of the series (kept beside the ledger for the record; with its switch off the five-patch tree was thirdjam, 600 of 600 hashes).
notes: What two rejected tries (E06 the coin, E08 the conditions) say together: the return is not held back by the mate's willingness. Half of the passes that arrive are lost by the mate before he does anything with them. The mates are thirdjam's plainest bots at every level (FJamBotSkill's defaults: no stick handling, no far-side carry), and pro's opponents strip them as soon as the half-second graces end. The pass will pay when a mate can keep a puck for a second, which is the mates' skill, not their intention. Epoch k8-4.
